text: To this trial Shakespeare had already been submitted. He had outlived his rivals and his patrons; and the century and a half that divided him from Johnson, though it had changed the taste, introduced new manners, and established new rules of writing, had not abated the delight which his works afforded. Johnson comprises the whole in a single image (Johnson 1765): "The stream of time, which is continually washing the dissoluble fabricks of other poets, passes without injury by the adamant of Shakespeare."
